entries.appliesTo: licensed mental health professionals/providers and any individual, corporation, or entity offering therapy or psychotherapy services in Rhode Island

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'unless the patient or the patient's parent, guardian or other legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following… (1) That artificial intelligence will be used; (2) The specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system that will be used'
dutySources.consent-workflow: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined in § 40.1-5.5-2'
dutySources.human-review: § 40.1-5.5-3(c) — 'A licensed professional or provider may not allow or otherwise use artificial intelligence to do any of the following: (1) Make independent therapeutic decisions; … (3) Determine therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans.'

sources.aiTherapyRule: § 40.1-5.5-3(b) — 'An individual, corporation, or entity may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet-based artificial intelligence, to the public in this state unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional or provider.'
sources.consentRequired: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined in § 40.1-5.5-2'
sources.scope: § 40.1-5.5-2(10) — '"Therapy or psychotherapy services" means services provided to diagnose or treat an individual's mental health or behavioral health.'
sources.enforcer: § 40.1-5.5-5(b) — 'The executive office of health and human services shall have authority to investigate any actual, alleged, or suspected violation of this chapter.'

flags: Confidentiality-of-records requirement (§ 40.1-5.5-4 — 'All records kept by a licensed professional or provider and all communications… shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as provided pursuant to the provisions of § 40.1-5-26') fits no listed duty key.

Penalties are imported by cross-reference, so no penaltyMax coded: § 40.1-5.5-5(a) — 'The penalties pursuant to § 5-37.3-9 shall apply to any violation of the confidentiality provisions of this chapter' — and apply only to confidentiality violations, not the whole chapter.
consent-workflow duty used for consent to AI use in therapy (the duty vocabulary lists likeness/replica/data use); closest available key.
§ 40.1-5.5-3(b) extends beyond licensed providers to bind any 'individual, corporation, or entity' offering AI-based therapy to the public — an unlicensed-practice ban alongside the provider duties.
Exemptions in § 40.1-5.5-5(c): religious counseling, peer support, public self-help/educational materials, FDA-cleared (or other federal-agency-cleared) AI tools, and IRB-approved research.

§ 40.1-5.5-3(a)'s consent trigger is conditioned on use of AI 'designed to simulate emotional attachment, bonding, or dependency or artificial intelligence companions' in supplementary support or therapeutic communication 'where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed' — a narrower trigger than all AI use.
